title: Last words: the useful remainder
intro: The final twenty: words too frequent to leave out that belong to no theme. The first entry is the best illustration in the book of gender carrying meaning — el orden and la orden are different words.

entries.warn: The gender changes the meaning outright. el orden is arrangement; la orden is an instruction, and also a religious order. Getting it wrong turns tidiness into a command.

ex.es: Los nombres están en orden alfabético.
ex.en: The names are in alphabetical order.
He carried out the order without asking.

entries.note: The second sense is informal and can be slightly dismissive.

ex.en: What kind of music do you like?

ex.es: Un tipo raro preguntó por ti.
ex.en: Some odd bloke asked after you.

entries.note: en punto means on the dot: a las tres en punto. estar a punto de is to be about to — see unit 49.

ex.en: That's the important point.
There's a full stop missing at the end.

entries.note: en línea means online; la línea aérea an airline.

ex.en: Sign on the line.

entries.note: Not a letter you post — that is una carta (see unit 12).

ex.en: It starts with the letter S.
He has very good handwriting.

ex.es: No me acuerdo de la letra.
ex.en: I can't remember the lyrics.

entries.note: See unit 33 for bands, unit 25 for school classes.

ex.en: They came as a group.

ex.es: Estoy en el grupo de la tarde.
ex.en: I'm in the afternoon class.

entries.note: al fondo means at the back or at the far end. en el fondo means deep down.

ex.en: The bathroom is at the back.
There was music in the background.
They set up a fund for scholarships.

entries.note: el nivel del mar is sea level; a nivel de at the level of.

ex.es: Su nivel de español es muy alto.
ex.en: Her level of Spanish is very high.

entries.note: ¿Qué edad tienes? is the formal way to ask; ¿cuántos años tienes? the everyday one.

ex.es: Está muy bien para su edad.
ex.en: He's in very good shape for his age.
What make is your car?

ex.es: Dejó una marca en la mesa.
ex.en: It left a mark on the table.

entries.note: mucho gusto is nice to meet you — see unit 5. con gusto means gladly.

ex.es: Tiene buen gusto para la ropa.
ex.en: She has good taste in clothes.
It was a pleasure to meet you.

entries.note: Countable, unlike English advice: un consejo, dos consejos. aconsejar is to advise.

ex.en: Can you give me some advice?

ex.es: El consejo se reúne el lunes.
ex.en: The council meets on Monday.

entries.note: hacer un esfuerzo is to make an effort; esforzarse to make an effort oneself.

ex.en: I really appreciate your effort.

entries.note: correr un riesgo is to run a risk; arriesgar to risk.

ex.en: It isn't worth the risk.

entries.note: apoyar is to support, both a cause and physically leaning something.

ex.es: Contamos con el apoyo de todos.
ex.en: We have everyone's support.

entries.note: hacer falta is to be needed — see unit 40. por falta de means for want of.

ex.es: Se canceló por falta de dinero.
ex.en: It was cancelled for lack of money.
It has three spelling mistakes.
The referee called a foul.

entries.note: llevar ventaja is to be ahead.

ex.es: Tiene la ventaja de estar cerca.
ex.en: It has the advantage of being close.

ex.es: La única desventaja es el precio.
ex.en: The only disadvantage is the price.

entries.note: paso a paso is step by step. Prohibido el paso means no entry.

ex.en: It's an important step.
The trees blocked the way through.

entries.note: dar la vuelta is to turn round or to go round. In Mexico la vuelta is also your change.

ex.en: I'll tell you when I get back.

ex.es: Dio dos vueltas a la plaza.
ex.en: He went twice round the square.
Keep the change.

entries.note: la meta is the finish line in a race, and a goal in life. el objetivo is also a camera lens.

ex.en: We met the year's target.
He crossed the finish line first.
